links.outcome: Sensitivity of single human reader plus AI versus double human reading on same screening data
links.effect: Combined single reading with AI recalled 5.0% (282 screen-detected cancers, 29 interval, 38 future) vs double reading 2.9%; sensitivity improved by 8.4% (95% CI 5.7-11.2, p<0.0001).
links.quote: Double human reading recalled 1244 mammograms (2·9%, 291 screen-detected cancers) and combined single human reading with AI recalled 2112 mammograms (5·0%, 282 screen-detected cancers, 29 interval cancers, 38 future breast cancers), improving the sensitivity by 8·4% (95% CI 5·7-11·2, p<0·0001).

links.outcome: Performance of human readers with versus without AI in intended deployment mode
links.effect: One human reader combined with AI detected more cancers than double human reading, independent of breast density, but recall rate rose from 2.9% to 5.0%.
links.quote: Evaluating screening mammograms with one human reader and AI leads to increased breast cancer detection compared with double human reading, independent of breast density.
